owner_decisions.quote: No, I think imp comes in during the final act, there should be a contest at the end that reflects part of the skill of the job that's a challenge against the imp
owner_decisions.meaning: The career's costumed imp stays hidden until the final act and enters when it begins. The final act ends in one head-to-head contest against the imp that exercises a skill of that job.

owner_decisions.quote: If imp wins, the game restarts immediately afterwards.
owner_decisions.meaning: The imp can win the contest. When he does, the contest restarts at once.
owner_decisions.interpretation_to_confirm: Implemented as restart_scope=contest_only: the contest attempt resets; earlier activities, stars, pearls, stickers and saves are kept. If the owner meant the whole career, change restart_scope to career.

owner_decisions.quote: The teacher should have an imp, but the game inverts, he teaches information that's wrong and it's your job to figure it out, which beats the imp. Similar educational type games
owner_decisions.meaning: The Teacher gets a visible imp. Its contest inverts: the imp teaches with deliberate mistakes, and the child beats him by finding each mistake and showing the right answer. Educational careers use the same inverted format.
owner_decisions.interpretation_to_confirm: The Teacher's inverted rounds reuse its four lesson kinds (pattern, count, add, match). 'Similar educational type games' is also read as covering the Geologist, the other learning career (FIELD GUIDE MIX-UP). If the owner did not mean the Geologist, it stays cooperative.

owner_decisions.quote: Lean into silly humor here, questions like, which smells the worst, farts, garbage, old diapers or rotten cheese?
owner_decisions.meaning: The imp's lessons are deliberately silly and gross-funny. The Teacher contest gains silly questions like the owner's example, and every imp line gets sillier.
owner_decisions.interpretation_to_confirm: Silly questions alternate with the math lessons rather than replacing them; the owner's smell question is used exactly and always comes first. If the owner wants the whole Teacher contest to be silly questions, only the round list changes.

shared.imp_starts_on: her first valid contest input (listening, demo and looking time never count)
shared.idle_pause_behaviour: if she has made no contest input for this long, the imp freezes (alternating taunt and guard), the existing rehint plays, and he resumes on her next input; zero input can never produce a win or a loss
shared.flub: exactly one scripted flub per attempt: the imp stops for about 2 s, plays his flub poses and his existing copy line; it is her comeback moment
shared.race_pacing: imp_units += delta * units_total / base_seconds * rematch_rate while active; ties go to Roshan
shared.points_rematch: the imp needs one more point per rematch, capped at +2; cues and shuffles run 25 percent slower after a lost attempt

imp_win_beat.then: restart the contest: reset both sides and the pearl rows, rematch += 1, Roshan says op_contest_again (new), she stays at her station (never walk back to a room object)

shared.player_win_beat: imp stagger then bopped then recover with his existing bop line, Roshan cheer; then the victory flourish phase if the career has one, else the curtain call where the imp bows
shared.score_display: reuse the existing header's two rows (hers above, his below) as wordless contest rows: discrete contests draw one pearl per unit or point (hers in the career accent, his in imp purple); continuous contests (paint coverage, racer distance) keep the existing bar; no numbers or text
shared.save: contest attempts are never saved: a resume always starts the contest from zero. Hall careers already checkpoint their phase index in opera_performance_checkpoints (save the contest phase with an empty current snapshot). Every other contest career gets the new additive dictionary key opera_phase_checkpoints = {career: {version: 1, phase_index: n}}, default {}, registered in save_state.gd DICTIONARY_KEYS and KNOWN_KEYS, written when a final-act phase arms and erased with the career's other checkpoints when the act is won (scripts/opera_house.gd:275-286). Leaving during the contest therefore never replays earlier activities.
shared.phase_naming: a replaced activity keeps its internal phase name (TOP, SHARE, BANDAGE, PICNIC, TITLE IMP, LAUNCH, RACE, BEDTIME, GEODE and the stage copy of GRAND TWIRL) because PHASE_STATIONS, HOTSPOT_PHASE_ALIASES, the hotspot catalog, voice keys and probes key on it; it gains a contest dictionary. Inserted contests (SPARKLE RACE, PAINT-OFF, HAT DUEL, SING-OFF) are new phases that need PHASE_STATIONS, hotspot, voice and probe entries. The contest names are design names, never child-facing text.
shared.mastery_hall: a rematch counts as one assist; a won contest still earns at least Bronze
shared.cheer_tier: by her winning margin: at least 0.35 of the contest ahead = 3, at least 0.15 = 2, else 1; any rematch caps it at 2; make it audible or visible, never text-only
shared.story_and_tutorial_runs: Chapter 2 story runs (reward_policy chapter2_story) and tutorial runs opt out: no imp and no contest

inverted_contests.shape: points contest in rounds; each round the imp presents one lesson or specimen with exactly one deliberate mistake and says it proudly (taunt)
inverted_contests.her_point: her first pick in the round is the right answer or the wrong part: his mistake pops off with a soft puff, the right answer settles in, he plays stagger then recover, imp line op_lesson_fixed
inverted_contests.his_point: her first pick is his wrong answer or another wrong answer: he plays hop_b then taunt with op_lesson_tricked; the golden help then shows the right answer (existing teacher_help clip) and she taps it to finish the round, scoring nothing
inverted_contests.hint: the hint button stays available; a hinted round scores for nobody and still ends with her placing the right answer
inverted_contests.truth_last: every round ends with the correct answer on the board, placed by her; his wrong answer is never left standing
inverted_contests.humor: silly and gross-funny, never mean: the joke is always on the imp or on the thing, never on the child or her family; he never calls her names and never says she smells; gross pictures stay cartoony
inverted_contests.clock: none: he never scores by time, so there is no idle pause and zero input never decides
inverted_contests.flub: none: every round is already his mistake
inverted_contests.rematch_mercy: his target +1 per rematch (cap +2); rounds step down one tier (never below 0); his wrong answer becomes the most obviously wrong choice
inverted_contests.save: attempts are never saved; the Teacher and Geologist keep using teacher_lesson_checkpoint and opera_geology_checkpoint for the phase index, with an empty mechanic snapshot on the contest phase

shared.imp_contact_rule: Each of his units must show readable contact with his own job object: the object sits at his hands, not floating above him; the unit lands on his slash contact moment with a small puff; he faces it. Alternating charge and slash beside a miniature picture is not sufficient. Captures must show the hand or tool touching the object.

player.round_note: Silly rounds alternate with lesson rounds; the first silly round of an attempt is the owner's smell question, then the silly list rotates from the total of teacher_learning_progress rounds so visits vary without a new save key.

silly_rounds.shape: Five picture cards: four that fit the question and one that obviously does not, which the imp picks proudly. Any fitting card is right (her choice among them is her opinion); the imp's pick is the only wrong answer.
silly_rounds.flow: The imp asks the question, naming the four fitting pictures as each one wiggles; he claims his pick (purple outline, taunt); her first pick decides the round. A fitting pick: he tests it (sniffs, listens, lifts, squeezes or tastes) with his reaction line, reaction poses and any sound, and she scores. His pick: his tricked line and his point, then the golden sparkle marks the four fitting cards and she picks one to see his reaction, scoring nothing. Hint: the sparkle marks the fitting cards and nobody scores.
silly_rounds.layout: five cards in one row on the lesson board (a new five-card branch in choice_rect, about 150 px wide on a 165 px step), positions shuffled each round
silly_rounds.mastery: silly rounds do not call record_result; they are not TeacherLessonPlan lessons

his_mistake.add: he presses the plus himself, the groups join, then he marks his wrong total card
his_mistake.match: he lifts his wrong shape card up beside the model shape

player.her_fix: She taps the right card. For count and add she first touches each pearl, exactly as in her lessons (the existing can_answer gate), and hears each number.
player.reuse: OperaTeacherSurface board, choice cards, pearl counters, join button, golden help and teacher_help clip; TeacherLessonPlan tiers

contest.imp_station: none: he teaches on her board; his wrong answer carries a purple outline and his pointer mark

imp.family_note: interim until the recommended rival_teacher family is approved; not the doctor costume the hidden Learning Buddy borrows today
imp.scores_when: her first pick in a round is wrong

contest.stand: at the right end of the board, about 150 px tall, feet near (1205, 640), clear of every choice card (the right-most card ends at x = 1133) and of the hint button at (1115, 150)
contest.mastery: each round calls TeacherLessonPlan.record_result(kind, assisted) exactly like a lesson: assisted is true when her first pick was wrong or she used the hint

new_imp_challenge.text: My turn to be the teacher! Can you catch my silly mistakes?

new_roshan_contest.text: The imp is teaching it wrong! Tap the right answer to fix it!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Hello, class! I'm the new teacher! I know everything! I think.

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Easy peasy, lemon squeezy! This one comes next!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: One, two, three... eleventy-twelve! It's this many!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Two plus one makes... a banana! No wait. This many!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Look! These two are twins! Same, same, same!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: You're the real teacher! I'll go sit in the silly corner.

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Which smells the worst? Farts, garbage, old diapers, or rotten cheese?

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: I know! This pretty rose! Pee-yew!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Pee-yew! That's so stinky! I'm gonna faint!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Hee hee! Tricked you! Roses smell nice!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Which is the loudest? A burp, a big drum, a roaring lion, or a fire truck?

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Easy! This teeny tiny mouse! Squeak!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Ow, my ears! That's so loud!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Hee hee! Tricked you! Mice are super quiet!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Which is the biggest? A whale, an elephant, a dinosaur, or a castle?

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: I know! This itty bitty ant! Look at its muscles!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Whoa! That's so big! I feel teeny!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Hee hee! Tricked you! Ants are tiny!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Which is the stickiest? Honey, bubble gum, a booger, or slime?

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: This fluffy feather! It sticks to everything!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Eww! My fingers are stuck together!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Hee hee! Tricked you! Feathers float away!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Which is the coldest? Ice cream, a snowman, an ice cube, or a penguin?

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Brrr! The sun! It's freezing!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Brrr! My toes are frozen!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Hee hee! Tricked you! The sun is hot!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Which is the slowest? A snail, a turtle, a sloth, or a slug?

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Zoom! This rocket is soooo slow!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Sooo... slooow... Yaaawn!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Hee hee! Tricked you! Rockets go zoom!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Which is the squishiest? Jelly, a marshmallow, mud, or a whoopee cushion?

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: This hard rock! Squishy squishy!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Squish! So squishy!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Hee hee! Tricked you! Rocks are hard!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Which is the yuckiest to eat? A mud pie, a wiggly worm, a stinky sock, or soap?

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Yuck! This cupcake!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Bleh! Yucky yucky yuck!

new_lines.speaker: imp
new_lines.text: Hee hee! Tricked you! Cupcakes are yummy!
